resource_containment_correction.v4_finding: two same-family findings: (1) the accepted caller's 4000ms timer starts at its CONNECT (window includes up to 1500ms connect phase; its connect timer clears at TCP-handshake completion, so accept can be deferred by backlog/event-loop beyond 1500ms) while the attester context starts at ACCEPT — so budget+margin<=4000 alone (and even total-connect-margin from accept) could let the attester sign after the caller expired; (2) request cancellation during provider() open was bounded by TIME only (clampRemaining), so a connection opened under a cancelled request became current and was reused.
guarantees_v4: caller-timeline is bounded by TWO layers combined via min: (a) accept-anchored budget = total - connect - margin = 4000-1500-600 = 1900ms (fail-closed load-time assert; both caller constants imported), and (b) a caller-timeline tightening after HMAC verify: ctx.tightenRemaining(total - max(0, now-ts) - margin) tied to the caller's authenticated ts, closing the accept-backlog gap for synced clocks; tighten-only (never extends), so a skewed/fast clock or crafted ts can only shorten the window

cancellation propagates INTO observer open: acquireObserver races provider() against a cancellation signal; a cancel/expiry while the open is unresolved abandons that generation — the returned connection is never admitted as current, is destroyed (in-flight via op.then/abandoned; resolved via the pre-current ctx.live() check), and the next request opens a fresh re-validated connection

supplementary delivery-boundary pre-sign guard: immediately before signer.issue the server checks the caller socket is still alive (!sock.destroyed) and refuses if the caller is gone, catching the close-wins-race case synchronously
still at most ONE outstanding open; bounded queue with expiry; stale/late results never signed; pre-sign authority gate; bounded shutdown — all preserved
